name: Talkspace Psychiatry
one_liner: Talkspace's online psychiatry: video visits with a psychiatric prescriber for non-controlled medications, by insurance or self-pay.
best_for: Adults with depression or anxiety who want medication managed by video
People already in Talkspace therapy who want medication in the same place
People whose insurance covers Talkspace psychiatry
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need controlled medications such as ADHD stimulants or benzodiazepines (Talkspace does not prescribe them)
People who need frequent in-person monitoring for complex medication regimens
short_description: Video psychiatry from Talkspace for non-controlled medications: $299 first visit and $175 follow-ups self-pay, or a copay with insurance.
long_description: Talkspace Psychiatry is the medication-management part of Talkspace, not a separate company. You see a psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner by video for an evaluation, and if medication is appropriate the prescription is sent to your pharmacy. Talkspace says it does not prescribe controlled substances, so stimulants for ADHD and benzodiazepines are not available. Follow-ups are about every three months. Without insurance the first evaluation costs $299 and each follow-up $175, billed separately from therapy plans; many insurance plans are accepted. Talkspace's published randomized trials studied its messaging therapy, not its psychiatry service. Universal Health Services completed its purchase of Talkspace in August 2026.
patient_summary: You book a video evaluation with a Talkspace psychiatric prescriber, who can prescribe non-controlled medications and send them to your pharmacy, then check in about every three months. Self-pay is $299 for the first visit and $175 per follow-up; with insurance you pay your plan's copay.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; $299 first visit, then $175/visit self-pay
pricing.notes: Psychiatry is billed per visit, separately from therapy subscriptions. Follow-ups are usually every three months. Controlled substances are not prescribed.

privacy.notes: Talkspace's US state privacy notice says it discloses personal information to third parties for analytics and advertising (you can opt out), but says it does not sell, share or target ads once you are a patient using the portal; care records fall under its HIPAA notice. Chat history can be deleted on request; medical records are kept as the law requires.

seo.title: Talkspace Psychiatry: Online Medication Management
seo.meta_description: Talkspace Psychiatry provides online medication management for anxiety, depression, ADHD, and more, starting at $199/month or covered by insurance.

faqs.q: Can Talkspace psychiatrists prescribe controlled substances?
faqs.a: Yes, Talkspace psychiatrists can prescribe controlled substances including ADHD medications and benzodiazepines where state law permits. Prescribing follows DEA telehealth guidelines. An initial psychiatric evaluation is required before any prescribing.

faqs.q: How much does Talkspace Psychiatry cost?
faqs.a: With insurance, copays are typically $25-75 per visit. Self-pay is $199/month for medication management only or $249/month combined with unlimited messaging therapy. Initial evaluations may have additional fees. Check insurance coverage before signing up.

faqs.q: How quickly can I see a Talkspace psychiatrist?
faqs.a: Initial psychiatric appointments are typically available within 1-2 weeks, much faster than traditional psychiatry wait times. Follow-up appointments can usually be scheduled within days. Emergency needs should go to local ER or call 988.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Talkspace Therapy and Psychiatry?
faqs.a: Talkspace Therapy provides unlimited messaging plus video sessions with licensed therapists. Talkspace Psychiatry is for medication management with psychiatrists or psychiatric NPs. Many people use both: therapy for ongoing support and psychiatry for medication. Bundle pricing available.

primary_uses: Medication management for depression and anxiety
Prescriptions sent to your local pharmacy

availability.note: Part of Talkspace (owned by Universal Health Services since August 2026). US only; no controlled-substance prescribing.
